steps.text: Place bacon in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat; cook until fat begins to render. Stir in onion and garlic; cook and stir for 1 minute.
Stir in beans and water. Cook until water has evaporated and beans are tender. Add more water as needed until beans are tender. Season with salt and pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Smothered Green Beans
raw_recipe.description: These green beans with bacon and onions are a flavorful holiday side dish quickly made on the stovetop with fresh green beans, garlic, and onion.
raw_recipe.name: Smothered Green Beans

review.reviewBody: Nice change from the traditional green bean casserole for the Holidays. Used a packaged thick sliced bacon and frozen whole petite green beans. Cooked the bacon whole first until it was crisp then removed from pan. As per other reviews only retained about 1 tablespoon of the grease. When I added the beans and the water I put a lid on the pan but left it cracked which allowed the beans that were not in the water to steam, while allowing the water to evaporate. When the beans were cooked and the water was pretty much gone, I returned the crisp bacon which I had chopped to the pan and tossed, put the lid on tightly and just let it sit for about two hours. I didn't want the beans to get mushy, but did want the bacon to soften up a bit. Right before serving I just heated it up. Everybody loved it - will definitely make again.

4 starts, because I changed the recipe, too. I cooked the bacon separately like everyone else, steamed the beans separately, as well, used a little grease, sautéed the onions and garlic, then added butter, maple syrup, bacon and beans. Yum!

Was a hit with two mods: first I cooked the bacon, onion, garlic mixture longer in order to avoid the bacon appearing muddled. This worked well. Second I added maple syrup with about 4 minutes to go. The syrup combined with the remaining water to create a sauce. I made way too much for a group of 10 and every last bit got eaten! Even the 3 and 5 year old ate them and wanted more!

This was really good! I used the fresh green beans and I did drain some of the bacon grease from the pan as other suggested here. I boiled the beans for just a few minutes in chicken broth and then blanched them before sauteeing. I saved some of the chicken broth and used that in place of the water. It was a top notch side for my pork loin!

This was really good. I changed it up a bit because I already had cooked bacon. I used some saved bacon grease to sauté the onions and garlic, then added beans. At about the 1/2 way point I added the chopped cooked bacon. To serve I added sautéed sliced mushrooms. It was delicious.

These beans were super tasty and full of flavor! I did change the cooking method and add in some fresh slices of red bell pepper. For the change in cooking method, I cooked the chopped bits of bacon about halfway through before adding in the bell pepper and onion slices and began cooking on medium-high heat for approx. 3-4 minutes. While the bacon, onion and bell pepper was cooking I added the fresh green beans into a separate pan full of about 3-4 cups of water and boiled them for about 5-6 minutes on medium-high heat until they were almost tender. I then drained the remaining water from the beans and added in the bacon, onion and pepper mixture to the beans along with the fresh minced garlic. I let the flavors mix together for a minute before adding in one cup of water and cooking the mixture for another 3 minutes on medium-high heat until the water evaporated. I then added in a few dashes of fresh ground pepper and a sprinkle of Kosher salt. The beans were full of flavor and still had a very mild crisp to them. They turned out perfectly with this method. I will be making them again in the future!

My gosh these are good! I made them today, and what a hit... It's already been suggested that I make them again. I followed some advise from others, and used chicken broth instead of water, just a couple tbls. of bacon fat, and added the bacon when the beans were done. I cooked the bacon crisp in whole strip, then broke it up in pieces and removed a lot of the fat. I used regular bacon - a pound of it (don't forget that I tore off almost all of the fat, so it really wasn't a whole pound). I cooked the bacon, onion, and garlic ahead of time, so all I had to do was cook the beans and add the bacon just before we ate.. Served to guests along with "Key West Chicken", also from this site, fresh corn on the cob, and a cold cabbage and pepper salad that I make. coffee, peach pie (also from this site), and vanilla ice cream topped it off. Fabulous dinner... thanks so, so much for sharing. You can bet I'll be making these again. Oh, what flavor!

I like the method of cooking where the liquid is boiled away instead of poured off, which keeps you from losing a lot of the nutrients from the beans. I would probably drain off a little bit of the fat next time, but love this recipe anyway. I doubled the recipe and used a whole pack of thick sliced bacon. I also used a can (2 cups) of chicken broth instead of water. I am usually not a fan of green beans at all, but I can't stop eating them! Will definitely cook again.

I used smoked bacon instead of normal bacon and cooked the beans separately , before I added them to the pan with the bacon , onion and garlic. I have cooked these several times now as my family refuse to eat green beans any other way
Make this with every holiday meal for the last 15 years! I even have them on my catering menu. Very easy and great flavor. I do cook them a little longer than called for.

I grew up with my mama making it exactly this way, and I'm 63 years old. Very good and I still make it to this day. Occasionally I will add boiled, till barely tender quartered red potatoes to the bacon and bacon grease and let them finish cooking with the beans. Also taught to me by my mother.

First, I'd like to say that it is totally unfair to give a lower rating when you change a recipe BEFORE even cooking it according to the written recipe. The first time I made these I followed the recipe exactly. I found it to be spot on as far as tasting like southern green beans. When I make a recipe for the first time I always follow the directions exactly with the ONLY EXCEPTION being the amount of salt called for, which in the majority of cases, I use way less. But in this particular recipe, it called for such a tiny amount that I used that amount. I will increase the salt next time to 1/2t.
Love this! I add a bit of lemon juice at the end.

Really liked this and it’s simple yet tasty. My small issue is that with only a min cook time, the bacon is hardly crispy at all and depending on how fatty your bacon is, a lot of bacon grease to sop up before adding the onions and garlic. I cooked my bacon closer to 5 min, using a paper towel to soak up some of the grease before adding the onions and garlic. If I could go back, I would have cooked a few min longer (likely closer to 10 min) so the bacon would have been more cooked. The water (I used chicken broth) doesn’t help it achieve the texture I prefer but does help make a nice “sauce” once cooked down. In the end, we liked this and paired well with our pork chops. Thanks Michelle O’Sullivan!

How is this recipe 5 stars? If you like steamed green beans, sure it's great. If you like dishes with flavor and texture, this is NOT it. I can't believe someone is using this for their catering company! Absolutely terrible. Do not make this.
My great grandma had a similar recipe without the garlic. She cooked it all day long on low. They were wonderful!
I've used a similar recipe from my great grandmother for years. Altho, great grandma cooked them low and slow for hours. They were so good!!
My husband loved this!
Loved It!! Best recipe for fresh green beans. I put some sliced mushrooms in it and it was great!
I cook my bacon in the oven until crispy, drain on paper towels and chop to add. I always have reserved bacon grease in my fridge so I use a small amount of that to make my sauce. Less greasy!!
